sentences.zh: 但由于他的健康状况，他拒绝了。

sentences.zh: 与此同时，霞飞知道了这一点，他拒绝让加利亚尼进驻他的总部。

sentences.en: He says to his aides, I can't stand him.
sentences.zh: 他对助手说，我受够他了。

sentences.en: He's always wound me up.
sentences.zh: 他总是惹恼我。

sentences.en: I suppose Galliani could say in reply that Joffre so far has had a shocker of a war.
sentences.zh: 我想加利亚尼可以反驳说，到目前为止，霞飞打了一场糟糕透顶的战争。

sentences.en: I mean, he's basically wiped out half the French army.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他基本上消灭了一半的法国军队。

sentences.zh: 他确实如此。

sentences.en: For nothing.

sentences.zh: 霞飞这场仗开局非常糟糕。

sentences.zh: 他这个疯狂的计划基本上害死了他所有的手下。

sentences.en: Max Hastings points out quite rightly, he says that if Joffre had basically died of a
sentences.zh: 马克斯·黑斯廷斯非常中肯地指出，他说如果霞飞基本上在9月1日死于

sentences.en: heart attack on the 1st of September, which is what Galliani expects at any moment, then history would remember him only as a bungler and a butcher.
sentences.zh: 心脏病发作——这也是加利亚尼随时预料的事，那么历史只会记住他是一个笨蛋和屠夫。

sentences.en: However, Joffre has one big thing in his favour.
sentences.zh: 然而，霞飞有一个巨大的优势。

sentences.en: He never, ever loses his cool because he's so large and he's always eating enormous lunches.
sentences.zh: 他从来、从来没有失去冷静，因为他体型庞大，而且总是吃丰盛的午餐。

sentences.en: He's very relaxed.
sentences.zh: 他非常放松。

sentences.en: So everybody else is completely panicking.
sentences.zh: 所以其他所有人都彻底恐慌了。

sentences.en: And he's actually just been sitting in silence thinking.
sentences.zh: 而他实际上只是坐在那里沉默地思考。

sentences.en: And to quote Max Hastings, that's an excellent line.
sentences.zh: 引用马克斯·黑斯廷斯的话，这是一句绝佳的台词。

sentences.en: His unbelievable calm is about to transfer him from, quote, abattoir superintendent to allied saviour.
sentences.zh: 他那不可思议的冷静即将把他从，引号，屠宰场总管转变为盟军救星。

sentences.en: Yeah, amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，真是惊人。

sentences.en: So first of all, he says, right, I'm going to sack all my officers.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，他说，好吧，我要撤换我所有的军官。

sentences.en: Like it's basically their fault.
sentences.zh: 就好像这基本上是他们的错一样。

sentences.en: So among them, he sacks that guy, Longerzak, who we talked about last time, the man from
sentences.zh: 所以在他们之中，他撤换了那个家伙，隆热扎克，我们上次谈到过他，那个来自

sentences.en: Guadeloupe.
sentences.zh: 瓜德罗普岛的人。

sentences.en: So his crime is to have been right.
sentences.zh: 所以他的罪名是猜对了。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: He's been right about everything.
sentences.zh: 他所有的事情都猜对了。

sentences.en: But Joffre says, basically, you lot are all tainted by failure.
sentences.zh: 但霞飞基本上说，你们这群人都被失败玷污了。

sentences.en: You've got to go.
sentences.zh: 你们必须走人。

sentences.en: And actually, I think that's, as it turns out, a good call.
sentences.zh: 事实上，事实证明，我认为这是一个明智的决定。

sentences.en: So he brings in a lot of new blood who are basically very energetic and desperate to prove themselves.
sentences.zh: 因此，他引入了许多新鲜血液，他们基本上非常充满活力，极其渴望证明自己。

sentences.en: But also, Joffre sees something that most people have completely missed.
sentences.zh: 但同时，霞飞看到了大多数人完全忽略的一点。

sentences.en: Most people at this point assume the Germans are going to win.
sentences.zh: 此时大多数人都认为德国人会赢。

sentences.en: The Germans themselves now think they're going to win.
sentences.zh: 德国人自己现在也认为他们会赢。

sentences.en: So one of their chief strategists on the 25th of August, a guy called Colonel Gerhard Tappen, tells his colleagues, he says, in six weeks, we shall finish the job.
sentences.zh: 因此，在8月25日，他们的主要战略家之一，一个叫格哈德·塔彭上校的人，告诉他的同事们，他说，六周内，我们将完成任务。

sentences.en: And that was the target, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是目标，对吧？

sentences.en: Of the Schlieffen plan, that it had to be done within six weeks.
sentences.zh: 施里芬计划的目标，那就是必须在六周内完成。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We will finish the French off and then we'll use the trains to get all our troops back to East Prussia, to Galicia, whatever, to deal with the Russians.
sentences.zh: 我们将消灭法国人，然后利用火车把我们所有的部队带回东普鲁士、加利西亚等地，去对付俄国人。

sentences.en: But Joffre, as he looks at these maps, he can see that the German offensive is now very, very stretched.
sentences.zh: 但霞飞在查看这些地图时，他能看出德国的攻势现在已经拉得非常非常长了。

sentences.en: So they have come an incredibly long way in a very short time.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在极短的时间内推进了极其漫长的距离。

sentences.en: In three weeks, they've travelled 200 miles and have thrust deep into France.
sentences.zh: 在三周内，他们前进了200英里，深入法国腹地。

sentences.en: But that's a problem for them.
sentences.zh: 但这给他们带来了麻烦。

sentences.en: Half of their lorries have broken down.
sentences.zh: 他们的一半卡车都抛锚了。

sentences.en: They're using thousands and thousands of horses to transport their supplies, or they're carrying their supplies, you know, physically carrying them themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们正在使用成千上万匹马来运输补给，或者他们正在运送补给，你知道的，亲自动手搬运。

sentences.en: Their horses are dropping dead with exhaustion.
sentences.zh: 他们的马匹因精疲力竭而纷纷倒毙。

sentences.en: Their men, who are not rested and rotated at all, there's no system for doing that, are carrying massively heavy packs.
sentences.zh: 他们的士兵根本没有得到休息和轮换，也没有这样的制度，却背负着极其沉重的背包。

sentences.en: They've all got, I'm very familiar with this issue, they've got new ill-fitting footwear that means they've got horrendous blisters.
sentences.zh: 他们都穿着——我对这个问题非常熟悉——他们穿着磨脚的新鞋，导致脚上长满了可怕的水泡。

sentences.en: It's very hot.
sentences.zh: 天气非常热。

sentences.en: And so they have begun to, A, to slow down, and B, to become very ragged and disorganised.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们开始，A，放慢速度，B，变得非常散漫和混乱。

sentences.en: So the further they go, the more mistakes they make.
sentences.zh: 所以他们走得越远，犯的错误就越多。

sentences.en: They get lost, they get jumbled up.
sentences.zh: 他们迷路了，搅成了一团。

sentences.en: They're basically making map reading errors.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上在读图上频频出错。

sentences.en: That's not very German, is it?
sentences.zh: 这可太不符合德国人的作风了，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is the thing, they're behaving in a very un-German way.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里，他们的行为非常不符合德国人的风格。

sentences.en: You could argue this was the fundamental weakness of the whole Schlieffen plan.
sentences.zh: 你可以认为这是整个施里芬计划的根本弱点。

sentences.en: It looks great on paper, but in reality,
sentences.zh: 它在纸面上看起来很美，但在现实中，

sentences.en: your laurels are going to break down.
sentences.zh: 你的军力将会崩溃。

sentences.en: Your men are going to get blisters.
sentences.zh: 你的士兵将会长水泡。

sentences.en: And the Schlieffen plan made no allowance for basically, you know, natural human failings.
sentences.zh: 而施里芬计划根本没有把自然的生而为人的人性缺陷计算在内。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this is a key element of war, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这是战争的一个关键要素，对吧？

sentences.en: You mustn't overextend your supply lines, and you have spotted this, whereas Schlieffen hadn't.
sentences.zh: 你绝不能过度延伸你的补给线，而你注意到了这一点，施里芬却没有。

sentences.en: You and I, and Joffre, are clearly cut from the similar, we're unflappable in that way, but we're not histrionic like a German general.
sentences.zh: 你、我和霞飞显然是同一类人，我们在那种情况下泰然自若，但我们不会像德国将军那样大惊小怪。

sentences.en: Having our lunch.
sentences.zh: 正在吃午饭。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Arrested History Scheduling Meeting, I think, is the technical term for a lunch.
sentences.zh: 被逮捕的历史安排会议，我想这是午餐的专业术语。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Now, the Germans are about to make a massive, massive misjudgment.
sentences.zh: 现在，德国人即将做出一个极其巨大的错误判断。

sentences.en: So, Molker's original plan was for them to go over the top of Paris and to encircle it, to go all the way around it and encircle it from the weSt. But in the last days of August,
sentences.zh: 因此，小毛奇最初的计划是让他们从巴黎上方绕过去并包围它，一路绕过巴黎并在西侧包围它。但在8月的最后几天，

sentences.en: the top German field commander, who's a man called Karl von Bülhoff, he decides, let's change the plan.
sentences.zh: 德国最高野战指挥官，一个叫卡尔·冯·比洛夫的人，他决定改变计划。

sentences.en: We probably don't even need to bother encircling Paris.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可能不需要费心包围巴黎。

sentences.en: And he says to the topmost bit of the army, so the right wing of the German army, which is under Alexander von Kluck, he says, don't bother going around Paris.
sentences.zh: 他对军队最高处的人，也就是由亚历山大·冯·克拉克率领的德军右翼说，别费心思绕过巴黎了。

sentences.en: Turn inwards before you get to Paris, kind of turn down towards the flank of the retreating British and French.
sentences.zh: 在到达巴黎之前向内转弯，有点像朝撤退的英法联军的侧翼转向。

sentences.en: Can I ask a question?
sentences.zh: 我能问个问题吗？

sentences.en: Is this because genuinely he thinks they don't need to bother enveloping
sentences.zh: 这是因为他真的认为他们不需要费心包围

sentences.en: Paris?
sentences.zh: 巴黎吗？

sentences.en: Or is it because they're all so tired and knackered that they think, oh, we'll just cut a corner?
sentences.zh: 还是因为他们都太累太疲惫了，觉得，哦，我们干脆抄个近路吧？

sentences.en: I think it may be a tiny element of both.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可能这两方面的原因都有一点。

sentences.en: They are very tired by this point.
sentences.zh: 他们到这个时候已经非常累了。

sentences.en: They are exhausted and they are very worried about their supply lines.
sentences.zh: 他们精疲力竭，并且非常担心他们的补给线。

sentences.en: But as well, they think, they assume the British and French, because they've been retreating so far, are beaten and they
sentences.zh: 但同样，他们认为，他们以为英法联军因为撤退了这么远，已经溃不成军了，他们

sentences.en: can just turn, sort of envelop them, squeeze them against their borders.
sentences.zh: 可以径直转向，将其包围，把他们挤压在边境上。

sentences.en: And we're talking about enormous armies and enormous distances and crush them between them.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是庞大的军队和巨大的距离，然后把他们夹在中间粉碎。

sentences.en: The battle of Cannae.
sentences.zh: 坎尼会战。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Instead of doing the whole plan, they will basically use Eastern France as their battlefield and they will envelop the Allied armies and crush them.
sentences.zh: 他们不再执行整个计划，而是基本上把法国东部当作他们的战场，包围盟军并将其粉碎。

sentences.en: So they crush the armies, they crush the armies and then Paris surrenders.
sentences.zh: 所以他们粉碎军队，粉碎军队，然后巴黎投降。

sentences.en: That's the plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是计划。

sentences.en: And then the French will have no one left and they'll have to surrender.
sentences.zh: 然后法国人将无人可用，不得不投降。

sentences.en: They won't even need to take Paris.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不需要攻占巴黎。

sentences.en: I have to say, I am massively, massively simplifying this because to emphasise, we are not.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我极大地、极大地简化了这一点，因为要强调的是，我们并非如此。

sentences.en: The rest is military history.
sentences.zh: 剩下的就是军事史了。

sentences.en: But the key point is that the German commanders have abandoned their original blueprint.
sentences.zh: 但关键点在于，德国指挥官们已经放弃了他们最初的蓝图。

sentences.en: They think the British and French armies are so broken, they just need to pursue and annihilate them.
sentences.zh: 他们认为英法军队已经彻底崩溃，他们只需要追击并消灭他们。

sentences.en: So now they are not following a sort of plan.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他们没有遵循什么计划。

sentences.en: They are basically making it up as they go along.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是走一步算一步。

sentences.en: And the key thing about this is that they are massively underestimating the Allies.
sentences.zh: 而这其中的关键在于，他们严重严重地低估了盟军。

sentences.en: And the reason for that, presumably, is the sheer number of people that you were talking about.
sentences.zh: 想必，原因就在于你刚才谈到的庞大的人数。

sentences.en: We're talking about hundreds of thousands, millions of people.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是几十万、数百万的人口。

sentences.en: So even if you wipe out, you inflict what seems countless numbers of casualties, you aren't necessarily breaking the capacity of an industrial nation to continue the fight.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使你消灭了，你造成了看似无数的伤亡，你也不一定能摧毁一个工业国继续战斗的能力。

sentences.en: I mean, is that essentially the misjudgment?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这本质上就是判断失误吗？

sentences.en: I think exactly.
sentences.zh: 我想完全如此。

sentences.en: I think especially a country like France, which is very highly militarised, which is basically now gone to an honour to a total war footing, is mobilising all its manpower.
sentences.zh: 我认为特别是像法国这样一个高度军事化的国家，它现在基本上已经进入了全面战争状态，正在动员其所有的劳动力。

sentences.en: There are a lot of Frenchmen left.
sentences.zh: 还有很多法国人在呢。

sentences.en: And France is a very serious country.
sentences.zh: 而且法国是一个非常严肃的国家。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can win these enormous battles in the Battle of the Frontiers, but there's still a long way to go.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，你可以在边境战役中赢得这些巨大的战役，但前方依然路途遥远。

sentences.en: And I think the
sentences.zh: 我想

sentences.en: Germans don't realise that, actually.
sentences.zh: 德国人实际上并没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: Because I guess the only war previously in history that would have taught that lesson would have been the American Civil War.
sentences.zh: 因为我猜历史上唯一能吸取这个教训的此前战争应该是美国南北战争。

sentences.en: Yes, I guess so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: Because the Franco-Prussian War was done and dusted pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 因为普法战争很快就尘埃落定了。

sentences.en: You know, they encircle and capture, they capture the Emperor, Napoleon III, and then it's pretty much done.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们包围并俘虏，他们俘虏了皇帝拿破仑三世，然后这事就基本结束了。

sentences.en: Whereas with this, you know, the canvas is so much bigger and the numbers are so much bigger.
sentences.zh: 而对于这场战争，你知道的，格局要大得多，人数也多得多。

sentences.en: I guess the Americans- But also the industrial capacity is so great and the supplies and everything.
sentences.zh: 我猜美国人——但工业生产能力也如此巨大，补给等等也是。

sentences.en: Yeah, railways, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 是的，铁路，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: The factories.
sentences.zh: 工厂。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And this is something that nobody really understands, I guess, at this point.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是此时此刻没有人真正理解的事情。

sentences.en: And it's also a testament, actually, to the French and the British have retreated 200 miles, but they have actually kept their discipline.
sentences.zh: 这也是对法军和英军的一种证明，实际上，法军和英军撤退了200英里，但他们实际上保持了纪律。

sentences.en: They haven't fallen apart in a complete chaotic sort of shambles.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有陷入彻底混乱的瘫痪状态。

sentences.en: They are very well-trained armies, by and large, and very cohesive.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，他们是训练有素且凝聚力极强的军队。

sentences.en: So they've actually managed to pull it off, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，他们实际上成功做到了这一点。

sentences.en: Now, then there's a big stroke of luck.

sentences.zh: 我想是没有的。

sentences.en: I think because the nature of it is you don't become a sort of Supreme
sentences.zh: 我认为其本质在于，你不到快六十多岁，

sentences.en: Commander type person until you're in your late sixties.
sentences.zh: 是不会成为那种最高指挥官类型的人的。

sentences.en: And at that point, people are quite, they've had a very unhealthy lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 而在那个时候，人们往往有着非常不健康的生活方式。

sentences.en: I think probably there's been drinking a lot of fine wines and it hasn't done any good.
sentences.zh: 我想可能平时喝了很多优质葡萄酒，而这毫无益处。

sentences.en: Late on the 8th, while he's talking to Hench, Bulow starts to get these more reports in the front.
sentences.zh: 在 8 日晚些时候，正当他与亨奇交谈时，比洛开始收到更多前线报告。

sentences.en: The allies are breaking through.
sentences.zh: 盟军正在突破。

sentences.en: And he says to Hench, my arm is being reduced to cinders.
sentences.zh: 他对亨奇说，我的军队正化为灰烬。

sentences.en: We're facing total catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 我们面临着彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: And Hench says to him, well, look, Molka has given me authority to say to you, if you want to retreat, it's your call.
sentences.zh: 亨奇对他说，你看，毛奇授权我对你转达，如果你想撤退，由你决定。

sentences.en: And this is the first time that anybody in the German army has really talked about retreating.
sentences.zh: 这是德国军队中第一次有人真正谈到撤退。

sentences.en: So this is a kind of landmark moment.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个具有里程碑意义的时刻。

sentences.en: They don't make the decision straight away, but overnight the mood gets bleaker and bleaker.
sentences.zh: 他们没有马上做出决定，但一夜之间，情绪变得越来越阴郁。

sentences.en: Three times Bulow breaks down in floods of tears.
sentences.zh: 比洛三次泪流满面地崩溃。

sentences.en: He says, you know, I can't cope with this.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，我应付不了这个。

sentences.en: I'm too stressed.
sentences.zh: 我压力太大了。

sentences.en: We're going to lose.
sentences.zh: 我们要输了。

sentences.en: My men are all going to die, all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我的手下都要死了，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: And at five o'clock in the morning, they get reports from air reconnaissance that the French are coming ever closer.
sentences.zh: 清晨五点，他们从空中侦察得到报告，法军正步步逼近。

sentences.en: And so at nine o'clock in the morning, at 9.02, in fact, we love a forensic fact, Hench says to Bulow, okay, fine, make the call, retreat.
sentences.zh: 于是早上九点，确切地说是 9 点 02 分——我们喜欢这种严谨的事实——亨奇对比洛说，好吧，行了，下达命令吧，撤退。

sentences.en: So Bulow, whose nerve is basically snapped now, issues the order for his second army to retreat.
sentences.zh: 于是，神经基本已经崩溃的比洛，下达了第二集团军撤退的命令。

sentences.en: So now Hench continues his driving tour of the front, the most disastrous drive in German military history.
sentences.zh: 接下来，亨奇继续他的前线驱车巡视，这是德国军事史上最灾难的一次驾车出行。

sentences.en: He drives 50 miles west to the headquarters of Alexander von Kluck's first army.
sentences.zh: 他向西驱车 50 英里，来到亚历山大·冯·克拉克第一集团军的总部。

sentences.en: It's a terrible journey.
sentences.zh: 这是一趟糟糕的旅程。

sentences.en: The roads are clogged with terrified refugees.
sentences.zh: 道路上挤满了惊恐万状的难民。

sentences.en: There are exhausted and wounded soldiers everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是筋疲力尽和受伤的士兵。

sentences.en: There's loads of artillery.
sentences.zh: 有大量的火炮。

sentences.en: There are wounded, you know, there's kind of men lying in the ditches, whatnot.
sentences.zh: 有伤员，你知道的，还有人躺在沟渠里之类的。

sentences.en: It's a complete war zone.
sentences.zh: 这里完全是一个战区。

sentences.en: And at various points, his car actually comes under attack from his own side because it's so, it's so confused and every order is broken down.
sentences.zh: 在好几个地方，他的汽车甚至遭到了自己人的袭击，因为局势太混乱了，所有命令都失效了。

sentences.en: He arrives at first army headquarters.
sentences.zh: 他抵达了第一集团军总部。

sentences.en: When he gets there, the first army officers are actually quite confident.
sentences.zh: 当他到达时，第一集团军的军官们其实相当自信。

sentences.en: They say, yeah, the British should come in, but we reckon we can handle the British.
sentences.zh: 他们说，没错，英军是进犯了，但我们认为我们能对付英军。

sentences.en: We've handled them before.
sentences.zh: 我们以前就对付过他们。

sentences.en: And Hench says, no, no, no, the second army is already retreating.
sentences.zh: 而亨奇说，不，不，不，第二集团军已经在撤退了。

sentences.en: So you probably need to fall back too.
sentences.zh: 所以你们可能也需要撤退。

sentences.en: And the first army officers are stunned.
sentences.zh: 第一集团军的军官们惊呆了。

sentences.en: They're like, what?
sentences.zh: 他们仿佛在说，什么？

sentences.en: We think we can win this.
sentences.zh: 我们认为我们能赢。

sentences.en: And he says, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，不，不。

sentences.en: Moltke has told me I've got authority to make these decisions.
sentences.zh: 毛奇告诉我，我有权做出这些决定。

sentences.en: You know, you should, you should pull back.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们应该，你们应该撤退。

sentences.en: So by the time he goes back to Luxembourg, the decision has actually been made.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他回到卢森堡时，这个决定其实已经做出了。

sentences.en: And later that day, the French advanced on where the second army had been, a place called Montmirail.
sentences.zh: 当天晚些时候，法军推进到了第二集团军曾经驻扎的地方，一个叫蒙米拉伊的地方。

sentences.en: And they're astounded when they get there because there's nothing there.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达那里时惊呆了，因为那里空无一人。

sentences.en: Von Bulov's second army has vanished.
sentences.zh: 冯·比洛的第二集团军已经消失了。

sentences.en: In their wake, they've left fields strewn with rubbish, including an unbelievable quantity of empty wine bottles, which probably tells its own story.
sentences.zh: 在他们身后，留下了散落着垃圾的田野，包括数量惊人的空酒瓶，这大概说明了一些问题。

sentences.en: The Germans have had a, you know, a final time in the, in the back of the battle.
sentences.zh: 德国人在战线后方，你知道的，度过了一段最后的时光。

sentences.en: The next day, the 10th is the same story further WeSt. So Max Hastings quotes a gunner
sentences.zh: 第二天，即 10 日，更西边的战况也是如此。因此马克斯·黑斯廷斯引用了一名炮手的话

sentences.en: called Paul Lantier, who had survived the slaughter at Verton in the Ardennes that we talked about last time.
sentences.zh: 名叫保罗·朗蒂埃，他曾在我们上次讨论的阿登地区韦尔通大屠杀中幸存下来。

sentences.en: This bloke Lantier's unit, they wake up and they just find it's really weird.
sentences.zh: 这个叫朗蒂埃的家伙所在的部队醒来后，发现情况非常诡异。

sentences.en: The birds are singing.
sentences.zh: 鸟儿在歌唱。

sentences.en: The sun is shining.
sentences.zh: 阳光在普照。

sentences.en: There's no guns.
sentences.zh: 没有枪炮声。

sentences.en: And a load of French infantry marched paSt. And the colonel of this unit marching past shouts, we've, you know, we've won.
sentences.zh: 大队法国步兵列队行进。走过的一位该部上校大喊，我们，你知道的，我们赢了。

sentences.en: The Germans are retreating all across the line.
sentences.zh: 德国人在全线撤退。

sentences.en: Lantier said afterwards, the news as it passed from mouth to mouth, shook us with joy, victory, victory, when we were so far from expecting it.
sentences.zh: 朗蒂埃事后说，消息一传十，十传百，巨大的喜悦让我们颤抖，胜利了，胜利了，在我们如此不抱希望的时候。

sentences.en: So the Germans have cracked.
sentences.zh: 所以德国人崩溃了。

sentences.en: The
sentences.zh: 法

sentences.en: French have won.
sentences.zh: 国人赢了。

sentences.en: And for the French, this becomes an absolutely legendary moment.
sentences.zh: 对法国人来说，这成了一个绝对传奇的时刻。

sentences.en: It achieves a kind of sacred status as the miracle on the Marne.
sentences.zh: 它作为马恩河奇迹，获得了某种神圣的地位。

sentences.en: And the guy who actually coined that expression,
sentences.zh: 而真正创造这个词的那个人，

sentences.en: unfortunately, at the end of the year was an ultra-nationalist, anti-Semitic writer called
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，在年底时，他是一个极端民族主义、反犹太主义的作家，名叫

sentences.en: Maurice Barres.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯·巴雷斯。

sentences.en: And he basically said that the miracle on the Marne, you know, this element that you talked about in the Angels of Mont's bonus, the supernatural, very important to sort of very
sentences.zh: 他基本上说过，马恩河奇迹，你知道的，你在《蒙斯天使》的红利中谈到的这个元素，即超自然力量，对于法国的

sentences.en: right-wing ultra-nationalist writers in France.
sentences.zh: 极右翼极端民族主义作家来说非常重要。

sentences.en: And he said, this is, I associate the miracle on the
sentences.zh: 他说，这是，我把马恩河的奇迹

sentences.en: Marne with, and I quote, the eternal French miracle, the miracle of Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 与——引述他的话——“永恒的法国奇迹，圣女贞德的奇迹”联系在一起。

sentences.en: The idea that, you know, in extremists, somehow, God will intervene and he will save France from the invaders.
sentences.zh: 这种观点是，你知道的，在绝境中，上帝会以某种方式干预，拯救法兰西免遭侵略者践踏。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, of course, the people who really deserve the credit are A, the French soldiers, and
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实上，当然，真正配得上赞誉的人是：A，法国士兵；

sentences.en: B, Galliani and Joffre, who in the crucial moment had not panicked, as their successors panicked in
sentences.zh: B，加利埃尼和霞飞，他们在关键时刻没有像后来的继承者们在 1940 年那样
陷入恐慌。

sentences.en: And Joffre, in particular, when he's sitting there eating his enormous lunches, he has chosen the right moment to strike back.
sentences.zh: 尤其是霞飞，当他坐在那里享用丰盛的午餐时，他选择了反击的正确时机。

sentences.en: I mean, his grasp of timing was perfect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他对时机的把握堪称完美。

sentences.en: But if you read most accounts of the Marne, actually, most historians are less interested in what the French got right, and more interested in what the
sentences.zh: 但如果你阅读大多数关于马恩河的记载，事实上，大多数历史学家对法军做对了什么兴趣不大，而对

sentences.en: Germans got wrong.
sentences.zh: 德军做错了什么更感兴趣。

sentences.en: You could blame the individual generals for changing their plan, but I think most
sentences.zh: 你可以把计划改变归咎于个别将军，但我认为大多数

sentences.en: historians would say the real problem is actually with the whole concept, the Schlieffen plan, or the Schlieffen
sentences.zh: 历史学家会说，真正的问题其实出在整个概念上，也就是施里芬计划，或者说施里芬-

sentences.en: Molker plan.
sentences.zh: 毛奇计划。

sentences.en: This idea of the six-week timetable was so unrealistic that there's probably no way that it could have worked unless the Allies panicked and lost their nerve.
sentences.zh: 这种六周时间表的构想太不切实际了，除非盟军陷入恐慌并失去斗志，否则它几乎没有成功的可能。

sentences.en: Basically, if the Allies kept their cool, the wheels were always going to come off the German juggernaut.
sentences.zh: 基本上，只要盟军保持冷静，德国人的这台战争巨兽就必然会车轮脱落、难以为继。

sentences.en: So can I ask, is there a sense, perhaps, that the commitment on the German part to this plan means that they are less able to
sentences.zh: 所以请问，德国人对这个计划的执着，是否意味着他们在临场应变方面

sentences.en: kind of think on their feet than they would otherwise have been?
sentences.zh: 不如平时那么灵活了？

sentences.en: It's an interesting question, because, of course, when they do think on their feet, it goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的问题，因为当然，当他们真正临场应变时，事情却搞砸了。

sentences.en: When they start to change the plan, I think that the truth of the matter is that the German plan is
sentences.zh: 当他们开始改变计划时，我认为事实的真相是，德国的计划

sentences.en: born of a really poor strategic position, which is your sandwich between France and Russia.
sentences.zh: 诞生于一个非常糟糕的战略地位，也就是你被夹在法国和俄罗斯之间。

sentences.en: And so they're probably right that the only, I mean, I suppose they could have just sat and done a defensive war and waited to be attacked by the Allies.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能认为唯一的——我的意思是，我想他们本可以坐视不管，打一场防御战，等待盟军来进攻。

sentences.en: But I mean, who wants to be attacked on two fronts?
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，谁愿意在两线作战中挨打呢？

sentences.en: I think they were probably right that in an offensive war, this was the only way they could win.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们在进攻战中认为这是取胜的唯一途径，或许是对的。

sentences.en: But it's just a massive, massive gamble.
sentences.zh: 但这只是一场规模极其庞大的豪赌。

sentences.en: I mean, would it have worked better if they'd stuck to the original and not improvised?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果他们坚持原计划而不即兴发挥，效果会更好吗？

sentences.en: But the improvisations are forced on them by the fact that the plan is simply impossible to stick to.
sentences.zh: 但即兴发挥是计划根本无法坚持下去这一事实强加给他们的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think to some extent you're absolutely right that they have to start improvising.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为在某种程度上你是绝对正确的，他们不得不开始即兴发挥。

sentences.en: And I think as well, maybe there is a psychological element.
sentences.zh: 而且我也认为，这其中可能存在心理因素。

sentences.en: To go back to your question, I think if you have been told we have to do this in six weeks, and this is the only plan that will do it, when the plan starts to go wrong...
sentences.zh: 回到你的问题，我认为如果你被告知我们必须在六周内完成，这是唯一行之有效的计划，当计划开始出错时……

sentences.en: Massive panic, yeah.
sentences.zh: 就会引发极大的恐慌，是的。

sentences.en: Well, this is exactly what happens.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这正是发生的事情。

sentences.en: So I think the Germans are probably psychologically much more shaken by their retreat from the Battle of the Marne than the Allies were by their retreat from the Battle
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，在心理上，德国人从马恩河战役撤退受到的打击，可能比盟军从

sentences.en: of the Frontiers.
sentences.zh: 边境战役撤退受到的打击要大得多。

sentences.en: Well, the British love a retreat, don't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，英国人喜欢撤退，不是吗？

sentences.en: You like going backwards, because you know you're going to win that way.
sentences.zh: 你们喜欢后退，因为你们知道这样最后能赢。

sentences.en: Well, you lose first, and then you retreat, and then you win.
sentences.zh: 嗯，先输，然后撤退，最后再赢。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's the story of all British history.
sentences.zh: 这就是所有英国历史的故事。

sentences.en: Because all the accounts that you have, the sort of diaries and letters, German officers are talking, and they say, you know, people are crying,
sentences.zh: 因为根据你们拥有的所有记录，比如日记和信件，德国军官们在交谈时说，你知道的，人们在哭泣，

sentences.en: they're devastated, they're confused, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们心碎欲绝，感到困惑，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I mean, here's a key thing, and I think it's really, really important in the long run in German history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里有一个关键点，我认为这对于德国历史的长期发展来说真的非常非常重要。

sentences.en: At this point, they didn't think they were losing.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，他们并不认为自己输了。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people in the Battle of the Marne thought they were winning, or that at least they were holding their own.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在马恩河战役中，很多人以为自己赢了，或者至少认为自己守住了阵地。

sentences.en: They didn't feel like a beaten army when they got the orders to go backwards.
sentences.zh: 当他们接到后退的命令时，他们并不觉得自己是一支被打败的军队。

sentences.en: So I think it's actually here, a month into the war, that you have in embryo the origin of a very poisonous political meme, I suppose, which is the idea we've been betrayed.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，正是从这里开始，在战争爆发一个月后，你萌生出了一个非常毒辣的政治迷因的起源，我想，那就是“我们被出卖了”的想法。

sentences.en: We've been cheated.
sentences.zh: 我们被欺骗了。

sentences.en: Okay, so stab in the back.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也就是背后挨刀。

sentences.en: We've been stabbed in the back by defeatists in high places.
sentences.zh: 我们被高层的失败主义者在背后捅了一刀。

sentences.en: Now, at this point, they're not talking in such explicit terms, and they're obviously not talking about, you know, communists, Jews,
sentences.zh: 当然，此时此刻，他们还没有用这么明确的词眼，显然也没有谈论，你知道的，共产党人、犹太人、

sentences.en: all the rest that they blame at the end of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 以及他们在第一次世界大战结束时所指责的所有其他人。

sentences.en: But there is this sense, we should have won.
sentences.zh: 但确实有这种感觉：我们本该赢的。

sentences.en: You know, we deserved victory, and for some reason, it has been denied us.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们配得上胜利，但出于某种原因，胜利被剥夺了。

sentences.en: And Dominic, where is the Kaiser in all this?
sentences.zh: 那么多米尼克，在这场风波中凯撒在哪里？

sentences.en: Is he hanging out with Molker?
sentences.zh: 他在和毛奇厮混吗？

sentences.en: The Kaiser's hanging around at the back.
sentences.zh: 凯撒在后方闲晃。

sentences.en: Obviously, he's as baffled and as confused and as angry as anybody, although he's not quite as devastated as von Molker is, because von Molker, who, as we've
sentences.zh: 显然，他和任何人一样感到困惑、迷茫和愤怒，尽管他没有冯·毛奇那么心碎，因为冯·毛奇，正如我们

sentences.en: said, is sickly and depressive and basically always on the brink of a breakdown.
sentences.zh: 所说，多病、抑郁，基本上总是处于崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: I mean, he's really taken this whole business incredibly badly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他把整件事看得极其糟糕。

sentences.en: And in fact, during the battle, during this period, he's been writing these extraordinary letters to his wife.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在战役期间，在这一时期，他一直在给妻子写一些非同寻常的信。

sentences.en: I cannot find the words to describe the crushing burden of responsibility that's weighed on my shoulders in the last few days.
sentences.zh: 我无法用言语来形容过去几天压在我肩上的那份沉重的责任感。

sentences.en: The appalling difficulties of our present situation hang before my eyes like a dark curtain through which I can see nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们当前处境的骇人困难就像一道黑色的幕布悬挂在我的眼前，透过它我什么也看不见。

sentences.en: The whole world is in league against us.
sentences.zh: 全世界都在联合起来反对我们。

sentences.en: It would seem that every country is bent on destroying Germany once and for all.
sentences.zh: 似乎每个国家都一心想要彻底消灭德国。

sentences.en: They're very self-pitying.
sentences.zh: 他们非常自怨自艾。

sentences.en: But also, there's a lot of guilt, actually.
sentences.zh: 但同时，其实也有很多负罪感。

sentences.en: He says, I feel sick to think of how many Germans have died.
sentences.zh: 他说，一想到有多少德国人死去，我就感到恶心。

sentences.en: Often, terror overcomes me when I think of this, and I have the feeling that I must answer for this horror.
sentences.zh: 通常，当我想到这一点时，恐惧就会战胜我，我有一种必须为这场恐怖负责的感觉。

sentences.en: I mean, this is very sub-ideal from your supreme commander.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对你的最高统帅来说，这非常不理想。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's not great, is it?
sentences.zh: 是的，这不太妙，对吧？

sentences.en: And when people go to his headquarters in Luxembourg, they're horrified by what they find.
sentences.zh: 当人们去他在卢森堡的总部时，他们被所见所闻吓坏了。

sentences.en: I mean, again and again, people say, God, he's a wreck.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们一次又一次地说，天哪，他成了一个废人。

sentences.en: He's a broken man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个心碎欲绝的人。

sentences.en: There's one general who turns up called Karl Einem.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫卡尔·埃内姆的将军出现了。

sentences.en: And Moltke just says to him, my God, you know, how could this have happened?
sentences.zh: 毛奇对他说，天哪，你知道的，这怎么会发生呢？

sentences.en: And Einem loses his temper with him and says, well, if you don't know, who knows?
sentences.zh: 埃讷姆对他发了脾气，说，好吧，如果你不知道，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: You should know better than anybody.
sentences.zh: 你比任何人都该清楚。

sentences.en: How could you have remained in Luxembourg and allowed the reins of leadership to slip from your hands?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能留在卢森堡，眼睁睁看着领导权从你手中溜走？

sentences.en: So a few days after the Battle of the Man, 14th of September,
sentences.zh: 所以在马恩河战役几天后，即9月14日，

sentences.en: Moltke really starts to lose it.
sentences.zh: 毛奇真的开始崩溃了。

sentences.en: He's sort of pacing up and down the room in a very agitated way, whistling through his teeth.
sentences.zh: 他在房间里焦躁地踱来踱去，从牙缝里发出嘶嘶的吹口哨声。

sentences.en: And basically, word gets back to Berlin.
sentences.zh: 基本上，消息传回了柏林。

sentences.en: People say to the Kaiser, you've got to fire him.
sentences.zh: 人们对德皇说，你必须撤了他。

sentences.en: He's got to go.
sentences.zh: 他必须走人。

sentences.en: He's lost it completely.
sentences.zh: 他彻底失控了。

sentences.en: So on the evening of the 14th, the Kaiser appoints a new supreme commander, a new chief of the general staff.
sentences.zh: 因此，在14日晚，德皇任命了一位新的最高指挥官，一位新的总参谋长。

sentences.en: And he is a much chillier character.
sentences.zh: 他是一个性格冷酷得多的人。

sentences.en: He is the Prussian war minister,
sentences.zh: 他就是普鲁士战争大臣，

sentences.en: Erich von Falkenhayn.
sentences.zh: 埃里希·冯·法金汉。

sentences.en: That's a good name.
sentences.zh: 这名字真不错。

sentences.en: I mean, we've mentioned this, like the falcon swooping down, but...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们提过这个，就像猎鹰俯冲而下，但是……

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now he is from a Prussian landowning family, which means he's a Junker.
sentences.zh: 现在他出身于普鲁士地主家庭，这意味着他是个容克贵族。

sentences.en: But actually, unusually, he's quite young for a top general.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，罕见的是，作为高级将领他相当年轻。

sentences.en: So he's only 53.
sentences.zh: 他只有53岁。

sentences.en: And he is greatly disliked by everybody else.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常不受所有人待见。

sentences.en: It will amaze people to hear.
sentences.zh: 听了可能会让人大吃一惊。

sentences.en: He's a lonely kind of saturnine kind of man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个孤独而阴郁的人。

sentences.en: Very acerbic.
sentences.zh: 非常尖刻。

sentences.en: Does he have death in his eyes?
sentences.zh: 他眼里透着杀气吗？

sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定有。

sentences.en: Cold eyes.
sentences.zh: 冰冷的眼神。

sentences.en: Churchill thinks he's brilliant though, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 不过丘吉尔觉得他很厉害，对吧？

sentences.en: Churchill rates him as the best of the the best of the German generals.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔认为他是德国将领中最出类拔萃的之一。

sentences.en: I think he probably is actually.
sentences.zh: 我想他大概确实如此。

sentences.en: I think Falkenhayn makes a series of pretty decent calls.
sentences.zh: 我觉得法金汉作出一系列相当不错的决策。

sentences.en: I think he knows what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他很清楚自己在做什么。

sentences.en: The other generals don't like him for what they call his mocking superiority.
sentences.zh: 其他将领不喜欢他，因为他们所说的他那种嘲讽的优越感。

sentences.en: So he thinks he's better than they are.
sentences.zh: 所以他觉得自己比他们都高明。

sentences.en: The Kaiser likes him though.
sentences.zh: 不过德皇很喜欢他。

sentences.en: I mean, he's spent a lot of time sucking up to the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他花了很多时间讨好德皇。

sentences.en: And Falkenhayn, he's smart.
sentences.zh: 而且法金汉很聪明。

sentences.en: He thinks it's always, I always thought it was going to be a long war.
sentences.zh: 他认为——我一直以为这将是一场漫长的战争。

sentences.en: He thinks our priority for Germany is what we have, we hold.
sentences.zh: 他认为我们对德国的优先策略是：占领的土地，我们就要守住。

sentences.en: We're probably not going to win this on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 我们大概无法在战场上赢得这场战争。

sentences.en: If we win this at all, we'll win it politically.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能赢得这场战争，那也只能通过政治途径。

sentences.en: Ideally, we're probably going to have to strike a deal with one of our adversaries, probably Russia.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，我们可能不得不与其中一个对手达成协议，很可能是俄国。

sentences.en: We'll have to fight the Russians to a standstill and then strike a deal with them.
sentences.zh: 我们必须把俄国人打到精疲力竭，然后与他们达成协议。

sentences.en: But in the short term, obviously the priority is to find a new defensive position.
sentences.zh: 但在短期内，显然首要任务是寻找新的防御阵地。

sentences.en: Now the Germans, like the British and the French before them, have not lost their cohesion.
sentences.zh: 现在，德国人同之前的英法两军一样，并没有失去凝聚力。

sentences.en: They retreat in very good order and they're nowhere near giving up.
sentences.zh: 他们以极好的秩序撤退，远没有到放弃的时候。

sentences.en: They're still inside French territory, remember.
sentences.zh: 记住，他们仍然身处法国领土之内。

sentences.en: They still control the industrial northeast of France.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然控制着法国东北部的工业区。

sentences.en: They still control the iron ore field of Lorraine, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们仍然控制着洛林铁矿区。

sentences.en: They don't want to give that up.
sentences.zh: 他们不想放弃这些。

sentences.en: So on the 12th of September, they call a halt just above the River Aisne in the northeast of France, on a long kind of chalk ridge north of the river.
sentences.zh: 因此在9月12日，他们在法国东北部的埃纳河上方停了下来，停在河以北一条长长的白垩山脊上。

sentences.en: Now the next day, the French and the British, in pursuit, cross the river after them.
sentences.zh: 第二天，进行追击的法军和英军渡过河去追赶他们。

sentences.en: And it's a very cinematic opening to the Battle of the Aisne.
sentences.zh: 这是埃纳河战役一个非常具有电影感的开场。

sentences.en: The British troops are kind of crossing on these pontoon, improvised pontoon bridges in dense fog.
sentences.zh: 英军士兵在浓雾中通过这些浮桥、临时搭建的浮桥过河。

sentences.en: It's like the attack by the orcs, or no, it's Gilead in the Return of the King film.
sentences.zh: 就像半兽人的进攻，或者不，是《王者归来》电影里的吉力马扎罗……不对，是吉力得。

sentences.en: I hope you're not comparing the British to orcs.
sentences.zh: 我希望你不是在拿英国人跟半兽人作比较。

sentences.en: I'm comparing the use of pontoon bridges and fog.
sentences.zh: 我在比较浮桥和浓雾的使用。

sentences.en: Important to put that on the record.
sentences.zh: 这很有必要记录在案。

sentences.en: But at this point, it has started to rain.
sentences.zh: 但就在这时，开始下雨了。

sentences.en: So the weather has broken.
sentences.zh: 所以天气恶化了。

sentences.en: The summer is over.
sentences.zh: 夏天结束了。

sentences.en: Now both sides at this point in previous wars, with it pouring with rain, they're absolutely exhausted.
sentences.zh: 现在，在以往的战争中，面对倾盆大雨，双方在此时都已经精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: They've been going back and forth across France.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在法国境内来回奔波。

sentences.en: In the Great Northern War, which we did recently on the show, they would have gone to winter quarters.
sentences.zh: 在不久前我们在节目中讲过的大北方战争中，他们早就进入冬营了。

sentences.en: Even Charles XII would have gone to winter quarters.
sentences.zh: 甚至连查理十二世也会进入冬营。

sentences.en: But these days, people don't go to winter quarters.
sentences.zh: 但如今，人们不再进入冬营了。

sentences.en: They keep going.
sentences.zh: 他们还在继续推进。

sentences.en: And one reason for that is basically, they don't need supplies in the same way.
sentences.zh: 其中一个原因基本上是，他们不需要像以前那样依赖补给。

sentences.en: They have tinned food.
sentences.zh: 他们有罐头食品。

sentences.en: They have bully beef and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 他们有咸牛肉之类的东西。

sentences.en: So they can just stay out there for as long as throughout the duration.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以一直待在前线，直到战争结束。

sentences.en: And so it's at the
sentences.zh: 正是在

sentences.en: Aisne, this point, in mid-September 1914, that three key features of the First World War really become apparent.
sentences.zh: 埃纳河，在1914年9月中旬的这个时刻，第一次世界大战的三个核心特征真正显现出来了。

sentences.en: So first of all, both sides now are relying very heavily on their artillery.
sentences.zh: 首先，双方现在都极大地依赖他们的炮兵。

sentences.en: The days of cavalry charges are over.
sentences.zh: 骑兵冲锋的日子已经结束了。

sentences.zh: 他们用炮弹连续几个小时猛烈轰炸对方。

sentences.zh: 在某些地方，你知道的，每隔几秒钟就会落下一发炮弹。

sentences.en: That's number one.
sentences.zh: 这是第一点。

sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我猜还有一件事，你提到这里是白垩土地，白垩土非常容易挖掘。

sentences.en: So do the spades come out at this point and the picks?
sentences.zh: 所以这时候铁锹和镐头就派上用场了吗？

sentences.en: So digging and it's raining, right?
sentences.zh: 所以开始挖土，而且还在下雨，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's not, it's wet, wet chalk.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是普通的土，是湿漉漉的白垩土。

sentences.en: You can dig it quickly.
sentences.zh: 你可以很快把它挖开。

sentences.en: And if you're a German infantryman holding your position under attack from the Allies, the obvious thing to do is to take out your trenching tools.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个德国步兵，在盟军的进攻下坚守阵地，最显 S 做法就是拿出你的战壕工具。

sentences.en: The Germans actually have better trenching tools than the Allies do.
sentences.zh: 德国人实际上比盟军拥有更好的战壕工具。

sentences.en: They've been practicing digging trenches for the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 他们在过去10里一直在练习挖战壕。

sentences.en: And of course they want to hold their positions.
sentences.zh: 当然他们想要坚守阵地。

sentences.en: They're not anticipating moving.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有预料到要转移。

sentences.en: So they dig very deep.
sentences.zh: 所以他们挖得很深。

sentences.en: And this is one reason why for the whole of the First World War, the German trenches are usually better than the British ones.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么在整个第一次世界大战期间，德国战壕通常比英国战壕更好的原因之一。

sentences.en: The Germans don't want to leave their trenches.
sentences.zh: 德国人不想离开他们的战壕。

sentences.en: Whereas for example, the British or the French, their expectation is that they will advance and move on to new positions.
sentences.zh: 而例如英国人或法国人，他们的预期是他们会向前推进并转移到新的阵地。

sentences.en: I've never really thought of that.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未想过这一点。

sentences.en: I've learned something.
sentences.zh: 我学到了新东西。

sentences.en: So, oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: That's, you've actually, you've actually, you've actually, you've actually gained something from the podcaSt. I have.
sentences.zh: 真的，你从这个播客里确实学到东西了。

sentences.en: That's lovely.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: That's lovely.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: First time in 700 episodes or whatever you've, it's been occasional a few times before this, but that's a very good insight.
sentences.zh: 在700集节目里还是头一次，或者之前偶尔有过几次，但这真是一个非常棒的见解。

sentences.en: That's a top insight.
sentences.zh: 这是一个顶级的见解。

sentences.en: So, well, I mean, it's not my own.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，这不是我原创的。

sentences.en: It's in every single book about the First
sentences.zh: 每一本关于第一

sentences.en: World War.
sentences.zh: 次世界大战的书里都有。

sentences.en: I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: It just never really registered until I heard it from your lips.
sentences.zh: 只是直到我听到你亲口说出来，我才真正领悟到。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Oh, that's lovely.
sentences.zh: 哦，太好了。

sentences.en: So, so that means that the character of the fighting now has fundamentally changed.
sentences.zh: 所以，这意味着现在战斗的性质发生了根本性的改变。

sentences.en: Waterloo a hundred years before done and dusted pretty much in a day, but there's no way that's going to happen again.
sentences.zh: 一百年前的滑铁卢战役基本上在一天之内就尘埃落定了，但这种情况绝不可能再次发生了。

sentences.en: These battles are going to take weeks or months.
sentences.zh: 这些战役将持续数周甚至数月。

sentences.en: And a lot of the time they will involve men cowering in their trenches from shell fire before the whistle or the bugle goes and they have to go over the top.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，士兵们只能在哨子或军号吹响、不得不冲锋陷阵之前，躲在战壕里瑟瑟发抖以躲避炮火。

sentences.en: So this is actually the third element of the First
sentences.zh: 所以这其实是第一

sentences.en: World War that is different from other wars, maybe not the American civil war.
sentences.zh: 次世界大战区别于其他战争的第三个要素，也许美国内战除外。

sentences.en: And it's a sense that this will never, ever end.
sentences.zh: 那就是一种战争永远永远不会结束的感觉。

sentences.en: It's a sense of interminable hopelessness.
sentences.zh: 那是一种无休无止的绝望感。

sentences.en: So now you have men, the scenes for the first time, they're pouring with rain, men are knee deep in mud, they're covered in dirt, they're hungry, they're exhausted.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你看到士兵们，这种场景是头一次出现，大雨倾盆，士兵们深陷泥潭，浑身污垢，又饿又累。

sentences.en: The British, you mentioned what they're wearing, the British have been wearing the same clothes since the Battle of Mons.
sentences.zh: 英国人，你提到了他们的穿着，英国人自蒙斯战役以来就一直穿着同一身衣服。

sentences.en: They haven't changed in all that time.
sentences.zh: 这么长时间以来他们都没有换过。

sentences.en: It's a lot of pubic lice.
sentences.zh: 有很多虱子。

sentences.en: Almost certainly.
sentences.zh: 几乎肯定的。

sentences.en: And of course, it's the same for all sides.
sentences.zh: 当然，对交战双方来说都是如此。

sentences.en: There's a quote, I can't remember which book this was in, maybe Max Hastings, Creston Anderson, a German soldier.
sentences.zh: 有一段引文，我不记得出自哪本书了，可能是马克斯·黑斯廷斯，或是克雷斯顿·安德森，记录了一名德国士兵的话。

sentences.en: He writes in his diary on the 28th of September, we all know we're on our way into the jaws of hell.
sentences.zh: 他在9月28日的日记中写道：我们都知道我们正走向地狱的血盆大口。

sentences.en: We aren't ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们已经不像我们自己了。

sentences.en: We're hardly human any longer.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎不再是人类了。

sentences.en: At most, we're well-drilled automatons.
sentences.zh: 充其量，我们只是训练有素的自动机器。

sentences.en: God, if only we could become human again.
sentences.zh: 上帝啊，要是我能重新变成人该有多好。

sentences.en: And he never did.
sentences.zh: 但他再也没能如愿。

sentences.zh: 两年后他在索姆河战役中阵亡了。

sentences.en: And that's the kind of sentiment I think you see a lot in the First World War, but you didn't see it so much in other wars where every day is different.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种你在第一次世界大战中经常看到的情绪，但在其他战争中却很少见，在其他战争中每一天都是不同的。

sentences.en: There's a tremendous variety.
sentences.zh: 有着巨大的丰富性。

sentences.zh: 而且有一种感觉，谁知道呢，战争可能下周就结束了。

sentences.en: This time, I think everybody knows this is not going to be over anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，我想大家都知道战争不会这么快结束。

sentences.zh: 这也是施里芬一直恐惧的事情。

sentences.zh: 从这个时候开始，我觉得这场战争的故事就是双方不断想出各种歪招，毒气、大规模的正面进攻、

sentences.zh: 坦克，所有这些不同的手段来试图打破僵局。

sentences.zh: 但德国人在圣诞节前夺取胜利只剩下最后一次机会了。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So why don't the Germans do what they've done to Belgium and go through Switzerland?
sentences.zh: 那为什么德国人不复制他们对付比利时的做法，直接从瑞士穿过去呢？

sentences.en: The Swiss, you can't underestimate the Swiss, I think.
sentences.zh: 瑞士人，你绝对不能低估瑞士人，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: A crack at the Swiss?
sentences.zh: 打瑞士的主意？

sentences.en: A crack at the Swiss?
sentences.zh: 打瑞士的主意？

sentences.en: That's the great question of history.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上的一个巨大疑问。

sentences.en: Why has nobody ever had a crack at the
sentences.zh: 为什么从来没有人想过去打

sentences.en: Swiss?
sentences.zh: 瑞士的主意？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe a Swiss listeners, if we've got any Swiss listeners, they'll be able to explain why.
sentences.zh: 也许有瑞士的听众，如果我们有瑞士听众的话，他们能解释一下原因。

sentences.en: Don't they all do military service?
sentences.zh: 他们不是都要服兵役吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they do.
sentences.zh: 对，他们是要服兵役。

sentences.en: But I'm just thinking, you know, the Germans could just say, you know, like they did with Belgium, we're really sorry, we've just got to go around the corner.
sentences.zh: 但我在想，你知道的，德国人本可以像对付比利时那样说，真的很抱歉，我们只是得借道拐个弯。

sentences.en: But I think it's actually hard to go through Switzerland, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但我觉得要穿过瑞士其实很难，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not like flat with loads of railways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那又不是到处都是铁路的平原。

sentences.en: I mean, although they have very good railways in Switzerland, but I think they're built for tourists rather than built for kind of a million men.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，虽然瑞士的铁路非常好，但我觉得那是为游客建造的，而不是为运送上百万军队建造的。

sentences.en: Well, I just throw it out as an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只是把它作为一个有趣的问题抛出来。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That's just not an angle I've ever...
sentences.zh: 这根本不是我曾经考虑过的角度……

sentences.en: So in all those books on the First World
sentences.zh: 所以在所有那些关于第一次世界大战的书籍中，

sentences.en: War, I've never seen anybody, you know, Max Hastings, all these great scholars.
sentences.zh: 我从来没见过任何人，你知道的，马克斯·黑斯廷斯，所有这些伟大的学者提到过。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, they haven't got my grasp on the operational level.
sentences.zh: 对，好吧，他们没有我对战役层面的那种理解。

sentences.en: That's what it is.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Clearly not.
sentences.zh: 显然没有。

sentences.en: Well, anyway, the trenches stretch all the way to the Swiss border, you can't go beyond that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不管怎样，战壕一直延伸到瑞士边境，你不能越过那里。

sentences.en: It's off limits, out of bounds.
sentences.zh: 那是禁区，是界外。

sentences.en: That's the rule.
sentences.zh: 这就是规则。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But above the River Aine, right, there is a 170 mile space to the channel.
sentences.zh: 但在埃纳河以北，对吧，到海峡有一百七十英里的空间。

sentences.en: If you could reach that, if you could go up around the trenches through this space, you could outflank your opponents.
sentences.zh: 如果你能到达那里，如果你能绕过战壕穿过这片空间，你就能迂回包抄你的对手。

sentences.en: And then maybe, you know, who knows?
sentences.zh: 然后也许，你知道的，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: You could get into their rear and cause all kinds of carnage.
sentences.zh: 你可以打到他们后方，造成各种血腥杀戮。

sentences.en: So for two months, for the next two months, there is what is called the Race to the Sea.
sentences.zh: 所以在两个月里，在接下来的两个月里，发生了所谓的“奔向大海”运动。

sentences.en: And the Germans are launching assault after assault, going over further and further north, trying to break through.
sentences.zh: 德国人发动了一次又一次的进攻，向北推进得越来越远，试图突破防线。

sentences.en: And the Allies are kind of catching up with them.
sentences.zh: 而盟军则在某种程度上追赶着他们。

sentences.en: They're kind of keeping pace with each other as they're going further north.
sentences.zh: 当他们向北推进时，双方的速度不相上下。

sentences.en: And they're sort of pushing them back.
sentences.zh: 他们有点在把对方逼退。

sentences.en: And so some of these battlefields,
sentences.zh: 因此，其中一些战场，

sentences.en: Albert, Arras, Tiepval, Messines, they become very famous kind of First World War names.
sentences.zh: 阿尔贝、阿拉斯、蒂耶帕尔、梅西讷，都成了非常著名的第一次世界大战的地名。

sentences.en: And by mid-October, this Race to the Sea has come down to the last bit of open territory.
sentences.zh: 到十月中旬，这场“奔向大海”的行动已经缩减到最后一片开阔地。

sentences.en: And these are the fields, the flat fields of Flanders, just south of the channel.
sentences.zh: 这些就是法兰德斯的平原，就在海峡的正南方。

sentences.en: And there's one town in particular that represents the last hope of a German breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 有一个小镇尤其代表了德国人突破防线的最后希望。

sentences.en: It's a medieval town.
sentences.zh: 那是一座中世纪小镇。

sentences.en: It's just inside the Belgian border.
sentences.zh: 它刚好在比利时边境以内。

sentences.en: It's just 20 miles from the sea.
sentences.zh: 距离大海只有20英里。

sentences.en: And its name, Tom, will become synonymous with the First World War, because this town is Ypres.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，它的名字将成为第一次世界大战的代名词，因为这座小镇就是伊珀尔。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So in our next episode, we will turn to the struggle for Ypres.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们的下一集里，我们将转向争夺伊珀尔的斗争。

sentences.en: Extraordinary story of heroism, but also of horror.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非凡的英雄主义故事，但同时也充满了恐怖。

sentences.en: And we will also be exploring one of the most controversial stories of the entire First World War.
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨整个第一次世界大战中最具争议的故事之一。
